channel.title: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers" - Have you joined the site because you want to write an SCP article or tale of your own, sometime now or in the future? Post your introduction here!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded: Hiya, I go by Hypastryx! I joined the site because I utterly love creative writing (Have been doing so for 6 years now) and SCP as a concept in and of itself always fascinated me. I *hope* as opposed to plan, to create one or more SCPs that are an interesting read, while also providing a more psychological side to the creatures/humanoids themselves that I create. I also love the atmosphere provided by a community with a set up like this, and even if my first ones divebomb I'm just thrilled to be here!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey DashDotBlank, and welcome to the site! Always great to welcome a long time fan to the ranks of members here. I like your attitude towards all this, and it's definitely a process to get an idea critiqued and reviewed before being able to even get to the drafting phase. With those kind of themes, I think you'll fit in just fine. As well as good taste in games, enjoy the gaming. Take your time and get acquainted with how everything here works, and make sure to check out IRC chat too!

For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5552

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

For posting ideas, make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you!

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.


Best of luck!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, fellow members. I am a freelance horror writer currently going to school at Full Sail U for creative writing. I was always a fan of the SCP genre of things, since long before I started writing. You could say, among other things, it somewhat inspired me to my own writing. And now that I am confident enough in my particular form of horror, I have decided to present myself among you all and begin the process of adding my own work to this glorious work of art we know as the SCP Foundation.

Personally, I have a deep and longing fascination with the horrors of the mind. This sprouted from an experiment I performed on myself with lucidity and the effects of uncontrolled experimentation. You see, the lucid state in which I brought upon myself didn't exactly stop when I wanted it to. It became abundantly clear to me that no matter what I did, I would eventually be conscious when I went to sleep. In this time spent in a lucid state, I began to feel as if I was being followed by something I had not created there. Or perhaps someone I had created unknowingly. Eventually, the method I had used to gain lucidity wore and with it, the state.

Nevertheless, I lay awake at night knowing that he… or it… is still in there somewhere.

Sorry if that was a little too much.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Greetings Foundation peoples!

I have been following SCP's for a very long time and have finally decided that I would like to contribute. For the most part I've just been lurking on the forums and viewing SCP content on Youtube but the creative juices have begun to flow and I must write them down somewhere! A lot of my hobbies involve creative writing (D&D, Hobby Game Design, Etc.) and this seems like a wonderful community to contribute to. Thank you all for leaving the door open for new members to join and the resources and guidance I've already had on IRC and other places. I look forward to my time on this site!

Best,

The Archivist.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello all.

I have never really tried for a community before so I am very happy being here, and thankful to you for having me. I am really looking forward to reading and writing for one of the best worlds ever created in fiction. I absolutely love the concept of the SCP universe and can't wait to be apart of it.

As for random thoughts that keep me up at night, I guess I have a very busy mind, too busy I suppose, most nights I'd just pace up and down my room thinking of stories I'll never write.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone,
I've been here reading for years now, but never built up the courage to actually join the community.
I'm currently working as a researcher in cognitive and behavioral neurophysiology, but I also moonlighted for a few years after high school as a playwright for local theaters. I sincerely hope that I can correctly mix my two writing sides, scientific and creative, in order to create something attractive and interesting. I already have some ideas, developed throughout the years, but, of course, quite a bit scared of community reactions.
As for what kind of random thoughts keeps me up at night, the answer is probably "stories", in the broadest and most general sense. I am enamored with stories so I spend hours thinking and ruminating fictional character and events. In a sense, it's like candy for my brain.
I sincerely hope to get immersed in the community. It's nice to be here, finally.

Hey Sniperhuman35, and welcome to the site! We are always happy to accept new members to the site, and I am always glad to see that there are still new people interested in this place. Take your time and get aquainted with how everything here works, and make sure to check out IRC chat too!

For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-3001

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

For posting ideas, make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you!

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.


Best of luck!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello Jabobai! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It's great to see you are as fascinated with the SCP Universe as we are here on-site. Hopefully your future readings won't disappoint you and will only make the feeling of wonder even greater. It also seems like you really want to contribute to the site, which I am very happy for; I can't wait to see what you come up with!

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hi all!

I found out about SCPs first on YouTube, where I first seen video about the SCP-173.
And there it escalated to 001 - When day breaks, 049 - the plague doctor, 096 - The shy guy and 106 - The old man.
Then I discovered that there is a game, SCP: Contaiment breach.
But that game wasn't fun for me because scp-106 and the fact that its horror game.
(Well I had fun when I turned on godmode and I played with peanut but thats for another topic.)
Then I found this site, the SCP wiki!
But my "ideas level" was at zero so I mainly only read scps.
Then I found another game, SCP: Secret lab.
I have at least fun in that game since is not that scary as scp:cb.
And im not hating on scp:cb Its just not my cup of tea.
Well I can say that SCP: SL put my "ideas level" to 10… and I wanted to write some scps.
So here I am! Ready to write some SCPs for the site.
Thanks to covid my hobby is… Well… Not existing.
So im looking into this as my new hobby.

The last thing that I can say is
Merry christmas!

(Also they should nerf 096 in secret lab. Im just sayin.)

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello, I actually jojned last month, but it took this long to figure out the work around for Chrome. Now that I'm here I have a few ideas, some are random SCP articles(which I will provide a brief list of in order to get feedback on which one you'd like to see first) and I want to introduce an OC to lay the groundwork for a movie and TV series. The OC is not going to be it's own SCP, rather it will be adapted from SCP-2806, specifically an arm that can double force/strength and has a retractable aramid covering. The individual this is attached to, SCP-2806-21A, is permitted to keep the arm in exchange for working for the Foundation as a member of MTF Alpha-9, an offer made when it managed to survive a security breach involving SCP-682 and actually helped recontain it. I need to figure out how to add an addendum to put this in, unless someone can explain the process better to me. The SCP article addendum would only include a description of the new instance, updated containment procedures and an interview between SCP-2806-21A and the agent that brought him in, other details will follow in tales that would connect to the Ressurection Canon, and by the nature of SCP-2806, create crossover with Those Twisted Pines.

+ show block
– hide block

Also I'd like to add to SCP-2923, Electric Lemonade flavor, the D-Class is now being used to power Site [REDACTED]

SPC-2806: cybernetics for pugilists who lost limbs in shark attacks so that they may once again punch sharks.

Other fun SCP ideas:
Playing with Fire - silly putty like substance that is plasma at room temperature, from Dr. Wondertainment.
Vampire Bodega - mini-mart where everything seems to be free, but actually draws blood from customers, not noticeable unless the customer comes more than twice a week. May be part of Marshall, Carter and Dark.
Cryovampire - cryogenically preserved person who was successfully revived, but now absorbs heat energy. Must be kept in a room heated to 98.6 degrees Farenheit at which point the ambient temperature neutralizes the anomaly, but as soon as it is exposed to lower temperatures it reverts to a savage that freezes anything it touches.
Alzoidian - a cephalopod like alien life form native to the red spot of Jupiter. Exists in symbiosis with a fungus and another species that resembles a manta ray. Still not quite sure how to explain how the foundation even acquired it…
Scapegoats - the acursed goats that carry the sins of the nation of Israel according to an ancient ritual.
Swine Legion - the accursed swine possessed by demons exorcised by Jesus.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Good morning, I'm Junior Researcher EJ. I have been lurking without an account for quite a while, reading through the SCPs, and now I'm hoping to introduce some of my own ideas at some point.

I intend on lurking a little longer and going through the guides before I muck out a proper idea for greenlighting territory, because I'm far from used to writing in the traditional file format and don't want to screw my first SCP up.

I'm hoping for some guidance and people willing to give both constructive critisms and maybe some tips and tricks in order to figure this new territory out. My interests tend to lie with the sapient SCPs and 'monsters', so that's likely where most of my writing will be headed, though I also intend to explore the object SCPs as well.

I…

… Have no idea what I'm doing. In the slightest. Any help, at all, would be greatly appreciated.

Hello hello NekoNeko_271! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey.

It seems you are quite interested in contributing to the site, which is awesome! If you want to get some help with your writing, especially the idea brainstorming part, you'll want to open that collapsible down below - there, you'll find a plethora of useful information that will help you with your writing her,e on-site.

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. It's a very helpful little place for when you want to start your writing journey, especially when you're not sure if the idea is all that great.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles. Within the Guides, you will find useful information written by experienced members of the site for the use of newer ones.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success! Remember - there is no rush to writing - take your time! The more time you spend on fleshing your ideas out, the more your chance of success becomes!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community to implement into your very own writing. Alternatively, you might want to look at the User Curated Lists page, where members of the community list and rank their favorite articles in different genres and themes, showing which attempts at such are successful and what the community likes.

Best of luck with your future contributions to the site! I hope you enjoy your time here as much as we do! If you have any more questions, feel free to message me here on Wikidot or on the IRC chats!
